They are refreshing their shoe collection and closet this weekend:
- Old sneakers currently in a shoe rack take up space and may smell. They will find a local cobbler through recommendations and online reviews or consider reputable mail-in services.
- To keep stored sneakers fresh: clean them first, ensure they are completely dry, maintain their shape with shoe trees/acid-free stuffing, use silica gel or baking soda/odor absorbers, store in breathable/dust-protected containers away from heat and direct sunlight, and check periodically for moisture or mold. Avoid sealing damp shoes in plastic.
- They plan to donate old dress shoes to a local charity thrift store Saturday. They will first check the charity’s guidelines or call ahead, clean/polish them, ensure they are wearable and free of broken heels, torn seams, excessive sole wear, or personal items, and pursue recycling or another charity if rejected.
- They want to inventory the whole shoe collection and donate, sell, repair, or keep each pair based on usefulness, comfort, and preference.
- Closet organization preferences: group shoes by type with dividers, keep frequently worn pairs accessible, store out-of-season footwear separately, and use space-saving vertical racks, shelf risers, or over-the-door organizers.
